Care of the affected area after gender reassignment surgery is important! Explanation of typical care and postoperative risks

2024 11/01
PR available
orchidectomy
September 30, 2024November 1, 2024

「How difficult is it to care for the affected area after sex reassignment surgery? ”

「I want to know what side effects there will be after the surgery.

Do you have such worries and questions?

Some transgender people who have been born with a sense of gender nonconformity may be considering sex reassignment surgery.

However, many people want to fully understand the effects on the body, such as the difficulty of post-surgery care and side effects, before making a decision.

Therefore, in this article,Introduction to affected area care after gender reassignment surgeryYaSide effects after gender reassignment surgeryI will explain in detail.

By reading this articleLearn about the hardships and risks associated with gender reassignment surgery, and use it as a basis for deciding on surgery.So please read to the end.

Table of contents

After sex reassignment surgery, you need to take care of the affected area.

After sex reassignment surgery,The affected area must be taken care of by self-disinfection and vaginal washing, which is painful.

In addition, movement restrictions usually last for about 3 to 4 weeks, and swelling and paresthesia at the surgical site may last for 6 months to 3 years, so it is essential to be prepared to face these symptoms for a long period of time.

As you can see, sex reassignment surgery places a heavy burden on you both physically and mentally, but once you overcome this, you can live your life as the person you are meant to be.

Please prepare thoroughly and deepen your understanding in advance so that you can go into surgery with as much peace of mind as possible.

Here, we will explain the difficulties of aftercare after sex reassignment surgery.

Aftercare after gender reassignment surgery
  • Dilation to prevent vaginal shrinkage | dilation
  • Hormone treatment continues
  • The urinary catheter will not be removed for a while after surgery.

Let's look at each one one by one.

Dilation to prevent vaginal shrinkage | dilation

If you undergo gender reassignment surgery from a male body to a female body,Extensive care called "dilation" is required to prevent vaginal contractions.It will be.

Dilation is to maintain the depth and diameter of the created vagina so that it does not narrow or close.

The frequency of dilation varies depending on the medical institution, but it is generally performed according to the following schedule.

Dilation is the process of inserting a rod-shaped device into the vagina, gradually increasing its size from thin to thick.

It may be painful, and some people may experienceI almost fainted from the pain.” It is a very difficult task.

The necessity and frequency of dilation will vary depending on the individual's constitution and the type of sex reassignment surgery, but please keep in mind that long-term care for one year or more may be required.

Hormone treatment continues

Hormone treatment, which is one of the physical treatments,Continues even after sex reassignment surgeryThis will be done.

Female hormones include the follicular hormone ``estrogen'' and the progesterone ``progesterone.''

These hormones are not secreted naturally even after a surgical transition from male to female, so they must be replenished regularly.

Continuing hormone therapy can provide the following effects:

  • breast size increase
  • skin becomes softer
  • Subcutaneous fat increases
  • decreased sexual desire
  • muscle weakness
  • Decrease in male hormones

The frequency of hormone treatment varies from person to person, but it is generally performed once every two weeks to once a month.

In order to prevent hormonal balance from being significantly disrupted after surgery, it is common to administer the same amount of hormones as before surgery.

If the amount of hormones is drastically reduced, hormone-related symptoms such as lethargy, headache, and palpitations may appear.

On the other hand, when the amount of hormones is too high, the risk of diseases specific to women, such as breast cancer and cervical cancer, increases.

Therefore, it is important to maintain a proper balance of hormones.

Hormone treatment isImportant not only for promoting physical changes but also for maintaining healthThat's it.

The urinary catheter will not be removed for a while after surgery.

After gender reassignment surgery, you will not be able to go to the bathroom for a while, soLeave the urinary catheter in placeThere is a need.

In sex reassignment surgery, the urethra is separated from the penis and a new urethra is created as a female genital organ.

As a result, it is difficult for the patient to urinate on his own for a while, and urination is controlled using a catheter.

To remove a urinary catheter, your doctor will check to see if you can fill your bladder and urinate on your own.

The urinary catheter cannot be removed until the bladder has filled with urine and the person can feel the urge to urinate.

It depends on the surgical method,If it recovers smoothly, it can be removed in about 10 days.There are many cases.

Also, keep in mind that you may feel pain when urinating for a few days.

3 side effects after gender reassignment surgery

Sex reassignment surgery and long-term hormone therapy come with some side effects.

Here, we will introduce three typical side effects.

Side effects after gender reassignment surgery
  • venous thrombosis
  • osteoporosis
  • breast cancer

By knowing the side effects after sex reassignment surgery, you can understand the risks that may occur after the surgery and make a careful decision whether or not to undergo the surgery.

Now, I will explain them in order.

1. Venous thrombosis

The female hormone ``estrogen'' isJapanese Society of Thrombosis and HemostasisAccording to the study, it increases clotting factors secreted by the liver.May increase risk of venous thrombosisIt is said that

Venous thrombosis is a disease in which blood clots called thrombi form mainly in deep veins.

In generalSymptoms such as edema and pain in one lower limbwill appear.

Furthermore, if this clot travels through the bloodstream to the lungs, it can cause a condition called pulmonary thrombosis, which can cause breathing difficulties.

Hormone therapy supplements both ``estrogen'' and ``progesterone,'' but in particular, by taking ``estrogen,''Risk of developing venous thrombosis increases by 1.3 to 3 timesI will.

Additionally, during the first year of taking estrogen, you are more likely to develop venous thrombosis, and the higher the estrogen content, the higher the risk.

For example, the powerful hormonal drug ``ethinyl estradiol'' is prone to blood clots, so care must be taken when using it as a contraceptive.

Risks vary depending on the patient's age, degree of obesity, smoking status, family history, etc.It is important to consult with your doctor regarding the type and duration of hormone medication.It is.

Oral female hormone pills are relatively easy to obtain online overseas, but it is dangerous to take them at your own discretion, so please refrain from taking them.

2. Osteoporosis

If the testicles, which produce male hormones, are removed, there will be almost no hormones in the body.

ThereforeDiscontinuing hormone therapy increases the risk of osteoporosis.

osteoporosisis a disease in which bone mass (bone density) decreases, making bones weaker and more prone to fractures.

Bones are constantly being regenerated, but a lack of hormones disrupts this balance and causes bones to become weak.

Bones are closely related to sex hormones, and the male hormone ``testosterone'' and the female hormone ``estrogen'' have the function of promoting bone formation.

Therefore,It is important to continue hormone treatment to maintain bone density and mass.That's it.

Osteoporosis is a disease that is difficult to recognize and is difficult to judge from appearance.

As a preventive measure, it is a good idea to visualize the amount of bone by regularly measuring bone density.

Also,It is important to maintain a nutritionally balanced diet with a focus on calcium-rich foods such as small fish and dairy products.It is.

3. Breast cancer

Administration of female hormonesYour risk of breast cancer may increase.

Breast cancer is a malignant tumor that arises from the epithelial tissue of the mammary gland, and is the most common cancer among women.

National Cancer Center Cancer StatisticsAccording to , the number of women diagnosed with breast cancer in 2020 was 91,531.

There is a close relationship between breast cancer and female hormones, and it is known that one of the female hormones, estrogen, promotes the growth of breast cancer cells.

However, estrogenIt is essential for maintaining a healthy femininity, such as maintaining a rounded body, beautiful skin, and bone mass, which are unique to women.

Therefore, it is important to administer appropriate hormones.

Additionally, factors that increase the risk of breast cancer include:

  • drinking
  • obesity
  • lack of exercise
  • diabetes

To prevent cancer, it is important to be aware of these risk factors and undergo regular breast cancer screening.

Cancer screening data from the Ministry of Health, Labor and WelfareWe also recommend breast cancer screening once every two years.

In order to maintain health after gender reassignment surgery, be sure to understand the side effects and risks, and take regular care and preventative measures.

Gender change requires loss of reproductive function

Many people who have undergone sex reassignment surgery not only have their bodies feminized;I want to change the gender on my family register and other identification documents to female.That's what I think.

This is because even if you look like a woman, you want to avoid revealing your gender identity disorder by presenting your ID.

In order to change the gender on the family register, a person must lose their reproductive function.

If you wish to change your gender, you will need to go to the family court in the area where you live to undergo a "trial for changing the treatment of gender."

In order for your gender change to be approved, you must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Be diagnosed with gender identity disorder by two or more doctors
  • Be over 18 years old
  • Not currently married
  • No current minor children
  • Absence of gonads or permanent lack of gonadal function
  • Having an appearance that approximates the genital parts of the other gender

Quote:Courts | Changes in the treatment of gender

When filing a claim, you must submit a doctor's certificate stating that you have gender identity disorder and the progress of your treatment.

If the judgment is approved, the gender on the family register will be changed and it will be possible to get married as the new gender.

You can also consider the option of eliminating only sexual function.
